summary: This RFC discusses how sites with several local links behind one gateway might organize them as subnets of an Internet network. It proposes a standard way of subnetting so the rest of the Internet need not care about internal details.

eli5.summary: A school has many hallways inside, but visitors only need the front door. This suggests a standard way to arrange the hallways.

questions: toward an internet standard for subnetting
how should sites organize local links as subnets
how does a host decide if a destination is on its subnet
subtitle: The GADS task force argues for one standard way to subnet, using a 32-bit mask to decide whether a destination is on the local subnet.

tldr.problem: Sites with several local links behind one gateway need hosts to decide whether a datagram stays on the local subnet. Without a standard scheme, hosts from different suppliers might not work together.
tldr.mechanism: A subnet field is taken from bits of the host (rest) field of the address, and each host uses a 32-bit mask with its own address to check if a destination is on its subnet.
tldr.outcome: Subnetting stays an optional local decision, invisible outside the network. The memo strongly suggests that anyone who subnets use this scheme.

facts.label: Test
facts.value: mask AND destination equals mask AND own address

today: The unit metadata gives no status for RFC 940 and records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The text is a discussion that proposes the subnetting scheme as the standard to use.

sections.title: Why a Standard Is Needed
sections.content:
Many sites have a complex of local links connected to the Internet through a gateway. The memo calls organizing each link as an entity like a network, joined by routing devices, subnetting. The links are subnets and the connecting devices are subgateways, bridges or gateways.

Every host must make the routing decision: is the datagram for a host on a directly connected subnet, or must it go to a gateway? Hosts come from various suppliers, so without a designated standard a customer using hosts from two or more suppliers may find they do not work together. The memo is by the Gateway Algorithms and Data Structures (GADS) Task Force, chaired by David L. Mills.
sections.eli5: If every toy maker used a different plug, the toys would not work together, so everyone should agree on one plug.

sections.title: The Subnet Field Approach
sections.content:
An Internet address had a two-layer hierarchy, a network and a per-network rest field. The scheme adds an optional subnet layer by stealing some bits from the rest (host) field. The details of the field are site specific, and all three classes (A, B and C) may be subnetted.

Using subnets is an optional local decision. A complex of links gets a single IP network number and looks like one network from outside, so no global change is needed. Any IP implementation that could be used where subnets exist should still provide subnet field configuration, because one without it will not work there. The memo does not require a particular implementation technique and does not specify how routing is done.
sections.eli5: The town only sees one front door. Inside, the building can split its house numbers into floors however it likes.

sections.title: The Mask Test
sections.content:
The example implementation uses a 32-bit mask with the host's own IP address. The mask can be set at boot time as a static quantity or distributed by a protocol that is beyond the scope of this memo.

If the bitwise AND of the mask with the destination address equals the bitwise AND of the mask with the host's own address, the destination is assumed to be on its subnet. If not, it is reachable only through a gateway. An all-zero mask makes every destination look local, an all-ones mask makes only the host itself look local, and a mask of ones in the network field and zeros in the rest field means subnets are not in use. For multihomed hosts the procedure applies per interface.
sections.eli5: The mask is a stencil laid over two addresses. If the visible parts match, they are neighbors on the same hallway.

sections.title: Related RFCs
sections.content: The background and rationale are in RFC 917, "Internet Subnets". The memo also cites RFC 925, RFC 932 and RFC 936 as part of the discussion of subnetting schemes.
sections.eli5: Other papers explain why this is a good idea, and this memo points you to them.
